transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-18
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Axiom CTO), Alex Rivera (Lead ML Eng), Maya Thompson (Head of InfoSec)
Shared items: Redwood quickstart guide (link), security pack (link), shared drive for prompts (note)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Samira, AE on the West coast. Lina is our SE who will run the bench side. Jordan, Alex, Maya, thanks for taking time. Should we go through agenda?
[00:18] Jordan (Axiom - CTO): Yeah thanks Samira. High level we want to see how fast we can get to first call, cost implications, and what it will take to move to an on‑prem/private setup later. We're evaluating multiple options so would like to be efficient.
[00:30] Lina (Redwood SE): Great — we'll do TTFT walk-through, show quickstart and free credits, then cover hosting modes and security. Also want to capture perf targets so we can run a bench.
[01:05] Alex (Axiom): Quick note — our app uses lots of short queries (20–60 tokens) and some long summarization flows (~2k tokens). P95 under 400ms is ideal for realtime features but we can accept higher for batch. Cost is a big factor.
[01:28] Maya (Axiom - InfoSec): From security side we need SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO + SCIM, KMS or HSM integration for keys, and audit logs retained for at least 1 year. Also data residency, EU storage for EU customers.
[01:52] Samira: Totally, we can cover those. We have SOC2 reports and KMS guidance in the security pack — I'll send. For quickstart, we provide free credits for pilot TTFT and Lina will provision a trial org.
[02:21] Jordan: How quick are we talking for first token? Our product team wants devs to be able to prototype same day.
[02:35] Lina: For self‑serve hosted API you can be calling in minutes — sign up, create an API key, run a simple cURL or SDK call. With our quickstart and example repo, many teams hit first token in under an hour. If you want Redwood Dedicated or private, setup time is longer — Dedicated has a provisioning window (days to a week depending on GPU pool). Private (VPC or on‑prem) is multi‑week for network and KMS integration.
[03:04] Alex: Any way to speed up Dedicated? We want predictable throughput for spikes but don't want to manage infra.
[03:18] Lina: Dedicated is reserved capacity — you commit to a pool and we map it, there's an onboarding checklist but we can prioritize. It's not a 1‑click move from hosted though.
[03:40] Jordan: And cost delta? Hosted vs Dedicated — rough guidance please.
[03:47] Samira: Hosted is pay‑as‑you‑go; unit cost can be slightly higher but no commitment. Dedicated reduces per‑token cost but requires monthly commitment. For pilot we usually recommend hosted with credits, then if you see stable traffic we talk Dedicated sizing. We'll share a sample cost model.
[04:20] Maya: On encryption — can Redwood integrate with our cloud KMS? We use a managed KMS with customer‑managed keys in AWS.
[04:33] Lina: Yes, we support external KMS integrations for private deployments; hosted tenants have options for keys via customer‑managed KMS for enterprise tiers. We'll include details — there's also an HSM option for Private.
[04:58] Speaker 1 (background): [inaudible]...
[05:12] Alex: One technical thing — our app relies on KV cache reuse across sessions, we need to make sure the prefix caching and KV cache is available or at least compatible.
[05:28] Lina: We support KV cache and prefix caching patterns in the runtime; sometimes transcription calls it K V cash, sorry the transcript often mangles that. For Dedicated/Private you get more control over cache eviction policies.
[05:52] Jordan: Good — on compliance, can you provide audit logs that show per‑token attribution and user‑level trace?
[06:03] Samira: Yes, our observability console provides per‑token traces, route‑level latency and token cost breakdowns. For enterprise we can surface token attribution and long‑term log export to your SIEM or S3 bucket.
[06:26] Maya: Retention windows — can we set retention to 1 year and have automatic export for compliance?
[06:36] Lina: Yes, for private deployments you control retention. For hosted we have enterprise add‑ons for extended retention and log export. We'll put the retention matrix in the docs.
[06:50] Jordan: Ok let's talk pilot — what would a minimal pilot look like?
[06:58] Lina: Typical pilot: 1) A small hosted tenant with free credits, 2) Run a benchmark with your 3 representative prompt sets (we'll provide a runner), 3) Measure P50/P95 latency and token cost with our default quantization profile, and 4) Review results to recommend Dedicated sizing or quantization tweaks.
[07:26] Alex: Are there sample runners or automation? We want reproducible bench results.
[07:33] Lina: Yes, we have a bench harness and we can spin up runs — simplest is to provide prompts and a call pattern and we'll run against our hosted cluster. If you want a private bench we'll need a lightweight agent.
[07:50] Jordan: How do we isolate data in hosted? We want strict isolation per customer.
[07:58] Samira: Hosted has tenancy isolation at logical level, data is segregated. For stricter controls and network isolation choose Dedicated (physical GPU pools) or Private (VPC, on‑prem). We'll map controls to your security requirements.
[08:24] Maya: Any certifications beyond SOC2? We also have customers that need ISO 27001.
[08:31] Samira: We have ISO 27001 and a compliance matrix — will include those artifacts.
[08:44] Alex: On the dev experience — do you have SDKs for Python and JS, streaming and function calling?
[08:53] Lina: Yes — REST + SDKs, streaming responses, tool calling primitives. We'll share code snippets. For TTFT, Python SDK + example repo is the fastest route.
[09:08] Jordan: If we start with hosted free credits and then need to move to Dedicated, how disruptive is that?
[09:17] Samira: Moving from hosted to Dedicated is mostly about routing and capacity. You can pin model versions and rollout policies so client code should not change much. There is some migration work on model endpoints and keys but we provide runbooks.
[09:38] Maya: Do you support SAML + SCIM for user provisioning into Redwood Console?
[09:45] Lina: Yes, enterprise accounts get SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync. We'll include docs and a quick SSO setup checklist.
[09:58] Jordan: Competitors — we're also talking to Anthropic and OpenAI. What would you say is Redwood's advantage?
[10:07] Samira: Our focus is production inference economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. We give control over batching, quantization guidance, and transparent performance dashboards. The observability and rollout controls are often cited by platform teams.
[10:29] Alex: Can you talk about token accounting granularity? We need per‑route breakdown to attribute cost to features.
[10:37] Lina: Per‑route, per‑token granularity is in the console; we can also emit token usage events to your billing system. We'll show sample exports.
[10:54] Jordan: For the pilot, what are the success criteria?
[11:02] Lina: Suggested criteria: P95 latency under 500ms for short queries, cost per 1k tokens under your target (you set threshold), and no data leakage issues — plus security checklist passed. If all meet, we recommend sizing for Dedicated or roadmap for Private.
[11:23] Maya: We'll need a short legal/data processing addendum for the pilot — minimal terms like data usage for benchmarking only.
[11:32] Samira: We can do a pilot DPA addendum for trial usage; legal can cut a short statement.
[11:45] Speaker 2 (murmur): [crosstalk]...
[12:05] Alex: A couple of technical constraints — we route some PII through the system; can we redact at the client before sending or does Redwood have redaction tooling?
[12:18] Lina: Client side redaction is best; we also offer post‑ingest scrubbers and field masking in Private deployments. We'll document patterns.
[12:35] Jordan: About costs again — can you share a modeled example for our estimated 5M tokens/month with mixed short/long queries?
[12:45] Samira: We'll prepare a cost model in the follow up. For now, yes hosted might be higher per token but no commit; Dedicated can substantially lower unit cost but requires commitment. We'll include a break‑even point example.
[13:09] Maya: Any notable limits on streaming or rate limits for trial?
[13:16] Lina: Trial tenants have generous rate limits for bench, but sustained production requires either Dedicated or rate adjustments. We'll give you the exact quotas in the trial onboarding note.
[13:34] Jordan: For EU data residency, can we keep all inference and logs in EU?
[13:42] Samira: Yes; we have region routing and can provision EU-hosted clusters or Private VPC in your region. We'll add regional residency notes.
[14:02] Alex: On the bench — can we run both default model and a quantized variant to compare cost/latency?
[14:10] Lina: Absolutely — we can run variants and provide quantization recommendations. That helps tradeoff cost vs quality.
[14:28] Jordan: How do rollouts and automatic fallback work if a model variant is overloaded?
[14:36] Lina: We have routing policies that can fallback to a compatible model variant or a higher‑latency but cheaper path; you can configure canaries and A/B routing in the console.
[14:53] Maya: Need to see logging to prove fallback behavior for audit.
[14:59] Samira: We'll include a trace example showing fallback events.
[15:18] Alex: One detail — how does rate limiting interact with guillotining long formation calls?
[15:27] Lina: We do continuous batching and token-level accounting; long formation calls are handled by configured SLOs. For real‑time features we tune batching to maintain low P95.
[15:48] Jordan: Ok good. I think next steps are clear. Quick recap?
[15:55] Samira: Yes: 1) I'll send security pack and SOC2/ISO artifacts (Samira), 2) Lina will provision trial org + API key and example snippets, 3) Axiom will share 3 prompt sets and P95 targets, 4) we'll schedule benchmark run.
[16:17] Jordan: Sounds good. Maya, Alex — anything else?
[16:22] Maya: Please include the retention/export options and a sample DPA for pilot.
[16:29] Samira: Will do.
[16:35] Alex: Also include a sample bench harness and the reproducible run steps.
[16:40] Lina: We'll attach the bench harness repo link and example config.
[16:48] Jordan: Great — if pilot looks good we may spin Dedicated in Q1, otherwise continue with hosted. Timeline wise we want results in two weeks.
[16:57] Samira: Two weeks is doable. We'll aim for bench results within that window.
[17:05] Speaker 3 (closing): [inaudible thanks]...
[17:12] Samira: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with notes and links. End of call.

Post‑call notes (auto):
- Samira to send docs and pricing (security pack link included)
- Lina to create trial org and share API key + SDK examples
- Axiom to provide prompts and target SLA
- Schedule bench run and agree pass/fail criteria
